\begin{abstract}
This report documents the implementation, evaluation, and analysis of an intelligent retrieval system for legal documents. The delivered artifact is a notebook that implements a self-contained pipeline including dataset preparation, indexing (TF-IDF example), an agent with query rewriting, intent classification, metadata extraction, retrieval, reranking, and answer generation. We present architecture diagrams, timing analysis, evaluation results, and practical instructions to reproduce the figures and tables.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
Accessing relevant legal knowledge is a core task for many applications. In this assignment we built a lightweight Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-style pipeline tailored to legal documents. The goals were:
\begin{itemize}
  \item Prepare and index documents (including guidance for OCR when needed).
  \item Design an agent that rewrites queries, classifies intent, extracts metadata, retrieves contexts with filtering, reranks results, and generates final answers.
  \item Measure per-node runtime and identify bottlenecks.
  \item Evaluate retrieval quality with simple metrics (answer relevancy, faithfulness).
  \item Provide a minimal user-facing wrapper (Chainlit skeleton).
\end{itemize}

\section{Dataset and preprocessing}
\subsection{Dataset}
For demonstration the notebook uses a small toy corpus of three Persian legal document headlines:
\begin{itemize}
  \item قانون جرایم رایانه‌ای
  \item قانون کار
  \item قانون مدنی
\end{itemize}
The final submission should replace the toy documents with the real dataset (download link provided in the assignment prompt). Documents which are stored as scanned PDFs must be passed through an OCR step (DeepSeek-OCR recommended) and validated manually.

\subsection{Metadata schema}
To support filtered retrieval (LanceDB or equivalent), the recommended metadata schema for each document/chunk is:
\begin{table}[H]
  \centering
  \begin{tabular}{lll}
  \toprule
  Field & Type & Description \\
  \midrule
  doc\_id & integer & Unique document identifier \\
  title & string & Document title \\
  year & integer & Year of publication / enactment \\
  source & string & Source (e.g., official gazette) \\
  jurisdiction & string & Jurisdiction scope (e.g., national) \\
  section & string & Optional: section or chapter name \\
  language & string & Document language (e.g., fa) \\
  \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
  \caption{Recommended metadata fields}
\end{table}

\subsection{OCR and validation}
For scanned PDFs:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item Use DeepSeek-OCR (or Tesseract for a baseline) to extract text.
  \item Validate by sampling pages and checking critical legal terms and numeric tokens (article numbers, dates).
  \item Apply lightweight normalization: Unicode NFC, remove control characters, normalize whitespace.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Indexing and embeddings}
The reference implementation in the notebook builds a TF-IDF matrix to act as a lightweight vector index so the entire assignment is reproducible offline. For production or improved retrieval quality use:
\begin{itemize}
  \item multilingual sentence embeddings (e.g. intfloat/multilingual-e5-large) to compute dense vectors.
  \item LanceDB or FAISS for efficient kNN search and metadata filtering.
\end{itemize}

\section{Agent design}
The agent implemented in the notebook follows modular stages:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item Query rewriting: normalizes and clarifies user queries.
  \item Intent classification: categorizes into Greeting, Abusive, or Law Question.
  \item Metadata extraction: extracts structured filters (e.g., year, keywords).
  \item Context retrieval: retrieves top-K documents using vector similarity and applies metadata filters.
  \item Reranking: sorts retrieved contexts and performs a relevance check; if top candidates are below a threshold, performs one retry with a relaxed filter.
  \item Answer generation: aggregates top contexts to produce an extractive/synthetic answer.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Pipeline pseudocode}
\begin{lstlisting}[language=Python, basicstyle=\small\ttfamily]
def run_pipeline(query):
    rewritten = rewrite_query(query)
    intent = classify_intent(rewritten)
    if intent != "law_question":
        return intent_response(intent)
    metadata_filter = extract_metadata(rewritten)
    contexts = context_retrieve(rewritten, metadata_filter, K=10)
    top = rerank(contexts, top_n=3)
    if not top:
        contexts = context_retrieve(rewritten, None, K=20)
        top = rerank(contexts, top_n=3)
    answer = generate_answer(rewritten, top)
    return answer
\end{lstlisting}

\subsection{Bottleneck and recommendations}
From sample timings the main bottleneck is \textbf{context\_retrieve} (kNN search / vector similarity). Recommendations:
\begin{itemize}
  \item Move to an optimized vector DB (LanceDB, FAISS) with approximate nearest neighbor search.
  \item Precompute and persist embeddings; serve them from memory or a fast index.
  \item Batch embedding requests and parallelize independent computations.
  \item Cache frequent queries and top results.
  \item For reranking, use lightweight neural scorers or re-rankers with small models hosted locally.
\end{itemize}

\section{Evaluation}
\subsection{Evaluation protocol}
We construct an evaluation set by sampling 3 QA pairs per document. For each question:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item Run the pipeline and save: question, predicted answer, contexts used.
  \item Compute answer\_relevancy as Jaccard token overlap (toy metric).
  \item Compute faithfulness as proportion of predicted tokens appearing in retrieved contexts.
  \item Export results to Excel (notebook writes \texttt{data/eval_results.xlsx}).
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Error analysis and discussion}
Common failure modes observed in experiments and expected in real datasets:
\begin{itemize}
  \item OCR noise produces incorrect tokens, hurting retrieval and faithfulness.
  \item Short or ambiguous queries lead to low recall in retrieval — query rewriting helps but may require paraphrasing models.
  \item Metadata extraction from queries can be brittle; using an LLM-based extractor or rule-based fallback improves filtering.
  \item Reranking threshold selection requires calibration per dataset to avoid unnecessary retries.
\end{itemize}
